Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a public holiday that falls on a weekday (Monday–Thursday) or on a weekend day (Saturday or Sunday) that creates a stretch of at least three consecutive days off.

| Date Range (2023) | Holiday(s) | Notes |
|-------------------|------------|-------|
| **Dec 31 2022 – Jan 1 2023** | New Year’s Day (Sunday) | The holiday fell on a Sunday, giving a 3‑day break that spills into 2023. |
| **Feb 20 2023 – Feb 21 2023** | Family Day (Monday) | Observed in Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, and Ontario. |
| **May 22 2023 – May 23 2023** | Victoria Day (Monday) | National holiday marking the birthday of Queen Victoria. |
| **Jul 1 2023 – Jul 3 2023** | Canada Day (Saturday) | The holiday fell on a Saturday, creating a 3‑day weekend. |
| **Aug 7 2023 – Aug 8 2023** | Civic Holiday (Monday) | Observed in most provinces (except Quebec). |
| **Sep 4 2023 – Sep 5 2023** | Labour Day (Monday) | National holiday. |
| **Oct 9 2023 – Oct 10 2023** | Thanksgiving (Monday) | National holiday. |
| **Dec 25 2023 – Dec 26 2023** | Christmas Day (Monday) | National holiday. |

> **Optional provincial holidays that also create long weekends in 2023**  
> • **Oct 10 2023 – Oct 11 2023** – Thanksgiving in Newfoundland & Labrador (falls on Tuesday).  
> • **Dec 26 2023 – Dec 27 2023** – Boxing Day in some provinces (falls on Tuesday).  

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app. If you need the data in a different format (CSV, JSON, etc.) let me know!
